holidays.name: Take Your Houseplant for a Walk Day
holidays.description: Pick up your ficus, tuck your fern under your arm, and give your leafy roommates a stroll in the fresh air. Expect a few double takes from the neighbors. Your plants will get some sunshine, and you'll get a great story.
holidays.origin: This lighthearted observance is credited to gardening authors Thomas and Ruth Roy, who also dreamed up other offbeat holidays. It has since been listed in Chase's Calendar of Events.
holidays.funFact: Plants don't need to be walked, but a short trip outdoors can be a nice change of scenery. Just keep delicate leaves out of harsh midday sun and strong wind.

holidays.name: National Walk on Stilts Day
holidays.description: Strap on some stilts and tower over everyone else for a day. It's a chance to try an old, wobbly form of transportation and entertainment. Stilt-walking can make you feel a bit like a circus performer.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It invites people to take a few elevated steps on July 27.
holidays.funFact: Stilt-walking has a long history. Stilts have been used for travel, for work and for performance in many cultures. Today they're a staple of street festivals and circuses.

holidays.name: National Crème Brûlée Day
holidays.description: This day celebrates the silky custard with a crackly caramelized sugar top. Tapping the surface with a spoon is half the fun. Treat yourself, or make your own with just cream, egg yolks, sugar and vanilla.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday, and its exact origin is unclear. It is observed every July 27, mostly by dessert lovers in the United States.
holidays.funFact: The dessert's name is French for "burnt cream." The classic version needs only a handful of ingredients, and a kitchen torch gives the sugar its signature crunch.
